Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Thornton, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Lisa Grant, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q3, we are proud of the significant strides NovaVolt Motors has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in charging network expansion and utilization rates, factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements, Average Selling Price or ASP trends by model and region, energy business revenue and profitability, impact of pricing strategies and promotional activities, cost reduction initiatives and their effectiveness, gross margin percentage and trends, and raw material sourcing and cost management. The market reception to our NV7 Max SUV has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated delivery volumes and customer loyalty far exceeding our initial estimates, driving repeat purchases and ecosystem engagement.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. Our revenue for Q3 reached $2.85 billion, marking an exceptional 25% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin expanded to 22.1%, driven by enhanced operational efficiencies, favorable product mix shifts, and robust energy segment contributions. Operating expenses amounted to $650 million, resulting in a net income of $180 million. Our financial position remains strong, with $3.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We anticipate revenue of $3.2 to $3.4 billion for the upcoming quarter.

To give you more color on the key drivers behind these results, let me start with our charging network expansion and utilization rates, a core growth engine as EV adoption surges worldwide. With the International Energy Agency noting over 14 million EVs on roads last year and forecasting a 17% compound annual growth rate through 2030, our SuperCharge network stands as a vital competitive advantage, fostering customer retention, steady revenue streams, and platform stickiness. In Q3, we added 4,200 SuperCharge stalls, pushing our global total to 28,500 across 3,200 locations—a 52% year-over-year jump that surpasses our annual target of 30,000 stalls. This rollout featured 1,800 next-generation V4 units delivering up to 350 kW peak power, now comprising 45% of our sites. We focused on major routes: in the U.S., 1,500 stalls went live along key interstates like I-95, I-80, and I-10, including collaborations with Pilot Flying J at 150 truck stops leveraging their vast network. Europe benefited from Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation requirements for 150 kW chargers at strategic points by 2025, adding 1,200 stalls with an initial 50-site deployment in Germany alongside Aral Pulse. In China, our SAIC joint venture installed 1,500 stalls in top cities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen to compete with State Grid's extensive public infrastructure. We're projecting another 10,000 stalls in fiscal 2024, backed by $450 million in capital expenditures and offering a three-year payback based on current usage patterns.

Shifting to utilization, our average daily rate rose to 38% in Q3, a 12-point improvement year-over-year and five points quarter-over-quarter, surpassing industry benchmarks like Tesla's 32% and Electrify America's 25%. Peak evening hours from 6 to 9 PM reached 72% occupancy, while average session times fell to 22 minutes due to our AI-powered queue management system, which cuts wait times by 40% through smart load distribution. This performance generated $185 million in charging revenue, up 68% year-over-year, with annualized revenue per stall at a record $28,500. Opening the network to non-NovaVolt vehicles via the NACS standard since February has been transformative, with third-party models like Ford's F-150 Lightning and GM's Ultium vehicles accounting for 22% of sessions and lifting overall activity without diluting our NV1 and Pro line sales. Charging gross margins climbed to 62%, from 55% last year, as fixed costs per kilowatt-hour dropped 18% with volume.

By region, North America, 65% of our footprint, averaged 42% utilization, supported by Inflation Reduction Act benefits and 95% uptime guarantees—California topped 48%, while Midwest expansions into underserved areas start at 28% but historically reach 35% within six months. Europe, 20% of stalls, hit 35%, gaining speed from EU Green Deal funding; the UK and Netherlands exceed 40% thanks to vehicle-to-grid trials with partners like Octopus Energy. Asia-Pacific, 15% and China-led, stands at 32%, enhanced by our Blade Battery's 800V setup achieving 3.5 miles per kWh efficiency, better than BYD's 2.8. Fragmented standards pose challenges in APAC, but our dual CCS2/NACS V4 ports address this.

On the innovation side, our SuperCharge AI platform employs machine learning for 92% demand forecasting accuracy, pre-conditioning batteries for 20% quicker sessions—such as 10-to-80% in 18 minutes for 100 kWh packs. Wireless 11 kW induction charging pilots with WiTricity are underway at 12 parking sites for continuous low-level use. Roaming pacts with IONITY and ChargePoint added 15% more sessions, and a $200 million Department of Energy grant supports 500 MW of solar-plus-storage at 200 U.S. locations, reducing peak grid expenses by 30% and opening virtual power plant opportunities via California's Low Carbon Fuel Standard.

Overall, the SuperCharge network contributed 28% to Q3 EBITDA with returns on invested capital over 25%. It's a self-reinforcing loop: better usage funds growth, which boosts vehicle sales—our charged customers exhibit three times the loyalty.

Next, our energy business revenue and profitability continue to shine as a high-margin pillar of our integrated ecosystem, including MegaVault industrial storage, PowerCore home systems, VoltSolar rooftop integrations, and our Virtual Power Plant software for vehicle-to-grid services. Q3 energy revenue hit $1.45 billion, up 162% year-over-year and 28% sequentially, on track for a $6.5 billion full-year pace—more than double prior year. We deployed 4.2 GWh, a 140% YoY rise, fueled by data center and utility deals, with a $12.3 billion backlog, 85% firm through 2025-2026 and $3 billion in letters of intent.

Margins expanded impressively to 29.8% gross, from 22.4% last year and 27.1% prior quarter—the sixth consecutive expansion—thanks to Shanghai Gigafactory scale on LFP cells below $55 per kWh and a shift to MegaVault at 62% of volume. Operating income reached $285 million at 19.7% of revenue, EBITDA at 24.2%—26% adjusted excluding R&D amortization—outshining our auto gross margin of 18.2%.

By product, MegaVault drove $920 million, up 210% YoY on 2.6 GWh, including a 1.2 GWh hyperscaler contract for AI facilities in Virginia and Texas amid Nvidia's GPU surge. PowerCore added $320 million, up 95%, with VPP aggregating 150,000 units in California and Australia for $45 million in grid service software revenue. VoltSolar contributed $150 million at 32% margins via IRA credits of $0.35 per watt, and SuperGrid fast-charging fees brought $60 million, up 45%.

U.S. led at 48% or $695 million, up 195% on IRA production and investment tax credits worth $450 million year-to-date, like an 850 MWh PG&E peak-shaving project. Europe was 28% or $405 million, up 130% under REPowerEU, deploying 1.1 GWh in Germany and UK with Orsted wind hybrids. China grew 75% to 18% or $260 million despite local rules, via Southeast Asia exports; APAC ex-China at 6% featured a 500 MWh Singapore grid deal.

Technically, MegaVault uses dry-electrode 4680 cells for 18% density gains to 280 Wh/kg and 25% lower capex per kWh. EnergyOS AI optimizes V2G at 99.2% accuracy, piloted on 5,000 vehicles in Texas for $12 million ancillary revenue. R&D of $180 million advances solid-state to 400 Wh/kg by 2026, with Redwood Materials recycling 95% cathodes.

Energy synergies with autos unlock $200 per vehicle annually in V2G; offtakes hedge 150,000 tonnes LFP precursor, 80% nickel for 2025. We see $10 billion revenue by 2026 at 30%+ margins, leveraging auto-scale cells.

Turning to gross margin percentage and trends, we posted 18.7% consolidated in Q3, up 250 basis points sequentially from 16.2% and 320 year-over-year from 15.5%—our best since the NV7 Blade SUV launch. This reflects manufacturing scale, supply resilience, mix, and pricing strength amid battery and chip fluctuations.

Year-over-year, 22% lower per-kWh costs from Nevada Phase 2 on LFP-NCM hybrids at $82/kWh versus $105 drove gains, plus 15% cathode savings via U.S. precursors avoiding lithium spikes that hit Rivian. Mix added 180 basis points with Blade SUV and Apex pickup at 45% and 30% volume carrying 22-25% margins versus Ion's 14%; premium ADAS Level 3 trims outsold base 3:1, lifting ASP to $52,000 up 8%. ZEV and IRA credits of $145 million added 110 basis points.

Sequentially, 28% delivery growth to 92,000 units spread fixed costs, with 82% U.S. factory utilization versus 71%, saving $1,200 per vehicle; localized Mexico shipping cut freight $220 million to $450/unit.

Regionally, North America at 68% revenue hit 21.4% on IRA $7,500 credits and 80% content; Europe 15.2% faced VW price pressure but Berlin LFP limited COGS rise to 3%; China JV at 12.8% countered BYD Seagull with Ion Lite targeting 50,000 H2 units.

Trailing trends show scale: 13.8% Q4 2023 trough to 18.7%, near Tesla's 19.8% ex-credits, ahead Ford Mach-E. Initiatives like cell-to-pack (12% material cut), giga-press ($800/vehicle save), FSD subs ($45 million 95% margin) underpin 20-22% FY25 guide, 25% by 2027 on 1.2 million run-rate.

On cost reduction initiatives and effectiveness, we've cut COGS 17% year-over-year to $28,500 for Apex 400 sedan, $42,000 for Max SUV, expanding gross to 24.8% up 420 basis points. Sequential 5% drop generated $1.8 billion run-rate savings, targeting $2.5 billion FY24.

Supply chain was 55% of savings: lithium to $28,000/ton locked via Piedmont/Albemarle; LFP ApexCell at $55/kWh, CTMP cut $1,200/vehicle. IRA domestic batteries subsidize 12%; Europe Northvolt 18% lower landed; China 25% edge.

Manufacturing 30%: GigaPress Reno cuts BIW 35% to $2,800; 92% automation ApexPack saves $900 materials, labor to $1,200; Shanghai OEE 88%, Berlin 85%; capex down 14% to $450 million.

Design 10%: Evolve platform 25% power electronics save; OTA 40% features defer $300 million R&D; sodium-ion pilots $40/kWh 2026.

SG&A 8.1% via zero-based, digital marketing $1,200 CAC.

Metrics: 23.5% FY margin guide; $1.2 billion EBITDA add to 12%; breakeven 450,000 units; 2.1% monthly COGS decline.

Next, we'll hear from Mike Thornton regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We have successfully implemented advanced automation technologies, resulting in increased production output and reduced cycle times.

Diving deeper, our factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements underpin this scalability in the EV arena, where Tesla pushes gigacasting and BYD verticalizes. We've committed $4.2 billion over 24 months to match Zephyr platform demand—outpacing Rivian's R1S 15% YTD—and Nova sedan H2 2025.

Nevada Gigafactory doubles to 80 GWh by Q4 2025 with four 46-series lines for LFP-NMC hybrid, 20% denser, 15% cheaper kWh; $1.8 billion cash/IRA funds 85% NA localization vs. 25% China tariffs.

U.S. Spartanburg 2 million sq ft plant nears 500,000 units 2026 from 220,000; Phase 1 95% uptime, 25 vehicles/hour Zephyrs.

Europe Debrecen Hungary 30 GWh mid-2026 for Nova structural packs, 16% recycled compliant; €450 million grants, 12% below Nevada via geothermal.

Asia Gujarat India JV Tata 20 GWh 150,000 units 2027 for sub-$30K, $200 million PLI.

Capex $1.1 billion Q3, 3.2x IRR on 25% EV growth.

Efficiency via Apex Lean 2.0: gigacasting 9,000-ton IDRA cuts Zephyr parts 70-to-1, 28% time/$1,200 COGS; Siemens NX OEE 82-to-94%.

Vertical e-axles/power electronics 60% self-supply cuts 18%; kanban inventory 45-to-22 days, $350 million WC.

Solar/waste heat 150 MW drops energy 22%, Scope 1 35% for CBAM/ESG.

Results: $2,800/vehicle cut 11% to $42,500 FOB; 35% QoQ to 125,000 units, Q4 150,000; EBITDA 14.2% to 18% FY25.

Modular 400-800V for 1.5 million 2028; LFP hedging/solid-state pilots.

Q3 capex $1.3 billion, FCF positive next year.

Following me, Dr. Vasquez will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, autonomous driving systems, and vehicle connectivity. We are committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that will redefine the future of mobility.

After me, Raj Patel will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network to mitigate risks and ensure the seamless flow of materials. Our proactive approach to supply chain management has enabled us to navigate the ongoing global challenges effectively.

Specifically on raw material sourcing and cost management—40-50% of COGS as we hit 200 GWh by 2026—lithium fell 82% to $14,500/ton post-2022 peak, nickel $16,000 down 30%, cobalt $28,000 stable; 22% QoQ input cut, $450 million bottom-line boost.

70% 2025-27 lithium indexed with Albemarle/Ganfeng at 60-70% LME; BHP nickel 150,000 tons $15,500 cap, 30% recycled Redwood IRA bonus.

China graphite/cathode de-risked 25% synthetic Northern/Group14 silicon-carbon +20-30% density; Norway/Finland EU act; Nevada Panasonic 85% IRA $1.2 billion PTC.

LFP 55% mix CATL Shenxing $52/kWh pack -18%; NMC dry electrode LG 20% lower; Li-Cycle 92% lithium $4/kWh credit 8% offset.

SDA Sila 1,200 Wh/L -12% mass $8-10/kWh; LMFP -40% nickel; SupplyChainOptix AI hedges 40% nickel $300 million save.

Baja copper 20%; DLE Lilac 90% recovery $4,500/ton; Scope 3 -28% RCS traced.

Costs 15-18% below 2023 '25; $1.1 billion FY25 savings fund 1 TWh.

Next, Lisa Grant will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Lisa Grant:
Thank you. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth. We are seeing strong demand for our vehicles across all regions, and we are actively pursuing new market opportunities.

In particular, on ASP trends by model and region, Q3 global fleet ASP was $48,200, down 8% YoY flat QoQ on entry-premium shift, mix-adjusted -6% ex-FX versus Tesla 9-10%, BYD sub-$20K.

185,000 vehicles +22% YoY.

North America 52% volume $62,500 ASP +4% YoY/2% QoQ; NV7 Max $72K 28% extended 102 kWh/FSD $12K; NV3 $45K IRA $7,500 65% net $68K; 15% premium configurator.

Europe 18% $55,800 -3% YoY flat QoQ €52K; NV7 Adventure $68K 800V 18-min charge vs VW 22; NV1 40% mix $38K post-subsidy; OTA winter +8% vs 7% FX.

China 22% $28,400 -15% YoY/5% QoQ RMB205K; NV3 Li RMB190K 65% base LFP; Shanghai cells -12% BOM RMB10K cut 18.5% margin; 14% share RMB200-250K.

ROW 8% $42,300 flat YoY +6% QoQ; NV1 $32K ASEAN; NV7 Brazil $58K flex.

Models: NV1 28% mix $35,200 -12%; NV3 32% $46,800 -7%/+1%; NV7 35% $58,900 +2% NA $72K; NVX 5% $105K +6%.

Drivers: 3 cuts vs Tesla 5, $4.2B incentives 1.8x ROI; cells $56/kWh -18%; SUVs 40% +$3.2K ASP.

Initiatives: AI configurator 5% Q4 lift; Evolve cuts variants 30%; India/Mexico $2B $48K FY25 ROW.

Q4 $48-50K +2-4% NV7 Pro 40K/month.

On pricing strategies and promotional activities amid softening demand, inventory pressures like Tesla's 100,000+, China wars, our discipline preserved EBITDA 12.4% -150 bps vs Rivian 8.2%.

ASP $48,200 -4.2% QoQ stable YoY; revenue +11% YoY $2.85B on 18% wholesale 72,000; premium 28% + OTA FAS $1,800.

Dynamic NovaAI 15 variables +220 bps NA share 9.8%; NA tiered $39,995-$72K vs Tesla $44K.

Europe €42,900 Bolt-E 10% below ID.3 +32% 25K; China RMB189,900 +1.2 pts 4.5% 14.2% margin.

$450M incentives 8% revenue: NA 1.9% APR $3K loyalty cleared 15K units 51 days conquest 42%; Europe €299 leases 35% 58% residuals; China warranties 22K -30% stock. ROI 3.8x.

Software subs FAS $99-199/month 65% margin 2025.

Q4 ASP $48-49K +15% 83K units 7-8% incentives.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, press star one one.

Analyst 1:
Thanks for the update. Jordan, could you expand on the charging network's role in customer loyalty and how it ties into overall ecosystem growth?

Jordan Hale:
Absolutely, great question. As I noted, our SuperCharge network is a flywheel—vehicles charged there show three times higher loyalty, driving NV7 repeat buys and energy product uptake. With 38% utilization and third-party access boosting sessions 22%, it's funding 10,000 more stalls while enhancing our moat against competitors. We've raised FY24 charging revenue to $750 million, directly supporting 28% EBITDA contribution.

Analyst 2:
Sarah, on the energy segment, what gives you confidence in the $10 billion 2026 run-rate amid potential auto demand softness?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks. Confidence stems from backlog $12.3 billion firm, hyperscaler/AI demand like 1.2 GWh wins, IRA/REPowerEU tailwinds, and auto synergies—V2G $200/vehicle. 29.8% margins from LFP scale under $55/kWh position us ahead of pure-plays, outpacing auto growth.

Analyst 3:
Mike, details on Spartanburg ramp and how expansions address tariff risks?

Mike Thornton:
Spartanburg Phase 1 at 95% uptime, 25/hour Zephyrs, full 500K 2026. IRA localization 85% shields 25% tariffs; Europe Hungary recycled compliant, India PLI hedges China. 3.2x IRR on BNEF growth.

Analyst 4:
Dr. Vasquez, any updates on solid-state or silicon anodes integration timelines?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
We're piloting solid-state with partners targeting 400 Wh/kg 2026, silicon-dominant anodes at 1,200 Wh/L now in 10% packs for $8-10/kWh save, LMFP reducing nickel 40%. Ties to 800V autonomy hardware boosting ASP upsell.

Analyst 5:
Raj, how are you managing lithium oversupply risks with your hedging?

Raj Patel:
Oversupply could hit $10K/ton, but indexed contracts 60-70% LME with floors/downside share protect; 70% lithium, 40% nickel hedged; recycling 20% 2026 offsets. DLE pilots $4,500/ton secure supply.

Analyst 6:
Lisa, ASP outlook with NV7 Pro launch—any mix shift concerns?

Lisa Grant:
Q4 $48-50K implies 2-4% growth on 40K/month NV7 Pro; SUVs to 40% mix +premium FSD 25% attach. AI pricing/dynamic bundles defend vs commoditization, margins +150 bps to 21%.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 7:
Jordan, overall gross margin trajectory to 25%—key risks?

Jordan Hale:
Margins to 18.7% Q3 on scale/cost-outs; FY25 20-22%, 25% 2027 via 1.2M run-rate, robotaxi ASP lift. Risks like price wars covered by 15% buffers, IRA tailwinds.

Analyst 8:
Sarah, cost savings run-rate—how much from LFP shift versus manufacturing?

Sarah Chen:
$1.8B run-rate: 55% supply/BoM like LFP $55/kWh CTMP $1,200 cut; 30% manufacturing gigacasting/92% auto; breakeven now 450K units, Q4 $27K/vehicle COGS.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
